fields.description:
## Problem
`review_bot/adapter.py::_translate_findings` maps each finding's kernel severity
(`critical/major/minor/none`) to the common vocabulary via its own copy of
`_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY`, but nothing downstream ever renders that value to a human:
`render_findings_block`/`_summarize` in `review_bot/finding_publish.py` render each finding as
`- ({criterion}) {detail}[ {location}]` with NO severity word anywhere, and the Gerrit comment
already conveys blocking vs advisory structurally (via the batch each call renders: `blocking`
items under one header, `advisory` items under another). So the human-facing Gerrit comment
ALREADY satisfies "blocking/advisory, never severity" -- `finding_publish.py` needs NO change.

The real defect: `_translate_findings` flattens `verdict["blocking"]` and `verdict["advisory"]`
into ONE list with no field distinguishing which bucket a translated finding came from -- its
`severity` computation is dead weight nothing reads. Separately, two CLI text renderers DO
print a severity word today, for findings that (after the sibling ticket
beaming-snively-urial) now also carry `priority`/`decision`: `_render_review_text`
(`review_result` findings) prints `f.get('severity','?').upper()`; `_render_plan_review_text`'s
advisory branch prints `sev={f.get('severity')}` (its blocking branch already prints no
severity). `_render_verdict_text` (completion_verdict findings) is OUT OF SCOPE: those
findings come from `completion_reconcile.py`'s independent module cluster, never pass through
the review-kernel, and never carry `priority`/`decision` -- `severity` is their only signal
and stays untouched.

`_render_review_text` is a SHARED renderer: besides code-review's `review_result` (from
`shim.py`, which now carries `decision`), it ALSO renders `scan_epics_for_spec`/`scan-spec`
results (`_llm_commands.py:222`) -- `spec_scan.py`'s free-form "spec-alignment" reviewer
findings, which never pass through the code-review kernel/shim.py and carry `severity` but
NEVER `decision`. A blind severity->decision swap would print a meaningless/fallback word for
every spec-scan finding and discard the only real signal that population has.

## Approach
1. In `review_bot/adapter.py::_translate_findings`, replace the `severity` key with a
   `blocking: bool` (`True` for items from `verdict["blocking"]`, `False` for
   `verdict["advisory"]`) -- fixing the genuine gap that the flattened output cannot currently
   tell the two buckets apart. Delete `_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY` from `adapter.py` (its only
   use site).
2. `review_bot/finding_publish.py` (`render_findings_block`/`post_review`) is NOT touched --
   confirmed it renders no severity word today and already conveys blocking/advisory via its
   `kind=` batching, satisfying the epic's human-facing design goal with zero code change.
3. Update `_render_review_text` in `_cli/_llm_commands.py`: when a finding's `decision` field
   is present (the code-review/`review_result` path), print `BLOCKING`/`ADVISORY` derived from
   it (`"block"` -> `BLOCKING`, else `ADVISORY`) instead of the severity word; when `decision`
   is absent (the `scan-spec`/`spec_scan.py` path), KEEP printing the existing
   `f.get('severity','?').upper()` fallback unchanged -- this renderer must serve both
   producers correctly.
4. Update `_render_plan_review_text`'s advisory branch to drop the `sev={severity}` suffix
   entirely (the function's blocking branch already omits any per-finding tag beyond its
   `[BLOCK ...]`/`[advisory ...]` bucket label, so dropping the advisory branch's severity
   suffix makes the two branches consistent -- no replacement tag needed since bucket
   membership already conveys blocking/advisory). Add a new test (none currently exists) that
   feeds a non-empty advisory finding through `_render_plan_review_text` and asserts the
   post-change line contains no `sev=` substring.
5. `_render_verdict_text` is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE (see Problem) -- left unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `grep -n "_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY" src/rebar/review_bot/adapter.py` returns no
  matches; `grep -n "_KERNEL_TO_COMMON_SEVERITY" src/rebar/llm/code_review/shim.py` still
  finds it (unchanged, out of scope for this ticket).
- [ ] `adapter.py::_translate_findings`'s output carries a `blocking: bool` key per finding
  instead of `severity`; `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_carry_forward.py -k test_adapter_carries_standing_through_to_the_receiver_shape`
  passes, strengthened with an assertion that a `verdict["blocking"]`-sourced finding has
  `blocking=True` and a `verdict["advisory"]`-sourced one has `blocking=False`.
- [ ] `src/rebar/review_bot/finding_publish.py` has zero diff from this ticket
  (`git diff --stat src/rebar/review_bot/finding_publish.py` is empty); `pytest
  tests/unit/test_review_bot_finding_publish.py` passes unchanged.
- [ ] `_render_review_text` prints `BLOCKING`/`ADVISORY` for a finding carrying `decision`, and
  still prints the uppercased `severity` word unchanged for a finding with no `decision` (the
  `scan-spec` case) -- a new test in `_cli/_llm_commands.py`'s test coverage (locate via
  `pytest --collect-only -q -k llm_commands`) asserts BOTH cases explicitly.
- [ ] `_render_plan_review_text`'s advisory branch no longer prints `sev=...`; a NEW test
  (none of the existing plan-review-reuse/gate tests cover this line -- they use empty
  advisory lists) feeds a non-empty advisory finding through `_render_plan_review_text` and
  asserts the rendered line contains no `sev=` substring.

## Testing
Tier: in-process unit tests against the real `_translate_findings` and CLI renderer functions,
fed production-shaped verdict/result dicts (contract test). Oracle: the exact
`blocking`/`BLOCKING`/`ADVISORY` values and text, asserted directly; and a negative check that
`finding_publish.py`'s rendered output is byte-identical to before (zero diff to that file is
itself the contrast/regression check). Contrast case (test-design.md sec.6): a `decision`-
bearing finding (code-review) and a `decision`-absent finding (spec-scan) fed through
`_render_review_text` must produce different label sources (derived-from-decision vs
severity-fallback) while both remaining meaningful. Refactoring litmus: renaming an internal
helper inside a renderer must not break these tests, since they assert on the printed
text/output value, not on which helper produced it.
